suggestedEngagement: The compute overcommit problem is real and unsolved — most sandbox vendors price on reserved cores but agent workloads are bursty by nature. Curious if @diptanu sees a path where vendors offer a burst-pool model, or whether this requires a fundamentally different pricing primitive (e.g., credit-based burstable pools rather than core reservations)?

Ask whether the 'backlash against sandboxes' is coming from the developer side (friction to onboard) or the enterprise buyer side (cost model unpredictability) — the remediation path is very different depending on where the resistance is.

description: A Stanford/MIT paper published in March 2026 demonstrates that changing the harness around a fixed LLM creates up to a 6x performance gap on the same model. The paper introduces Meta-Harness — an agentic system that automatically optimizes system prompts, tool definitions, retry logic, and context management. Key result: +7.7 points on text classification, 4x fewer tokens, #1 ranking on IMO-level math reasoning. Active X discussion today from @LiorOnAI (113.8K followers — above cap), @alex_prompter, and @omarsar0. suggestedEngagementAngles: The 6x performance gap from harness changes alone is the most important finding — it reframes where engineering effort should go. For production agent teams, this validates investing in harness iteration over model upgrades. Ask practitioners how they're currently approaching harness versioning and evaluation.

The 10M tokens per step (400x more context than prior methods) in Meta-Harness is what enables the failure trace back to exact line — this is a new observability primitive for agentic systems. The implication for enterprise deployments: harness debugging becomes tractable at scale.

The cross-model generalization result (single harness improves accuracy across 5 held-out models) is the enterprise-relevant finding — it means harness optimization is durable across model updates, which changes the ROI calculus for harness engineering investment.
